Never turn persistence failure into completed.
terminalPersistenceBatch.quitVersusReset: Normal quit may proceed after all real workers drain while retaining original files/last journal and logging the persistence warning. FactoryReset must reject marker publication/exit when this persistence error remains. Root owns common quit/reset admission and warning integration.

batches.design: A failed/interrupted live job retries finalization of its own durable segment manifest only; never silently records a later broadcast. The same archive job is revision-guarded and queued through bounded workers. Each merge attempt has a fresh filename, existing partial/final files are not overwritten, and published-before-journal crashes revalidate the existing final. Full verification precedes exact-owned segment cleanup; chat is retained and flushed even when its receiver fails.

batches.design: A single managed yt-dlp process resolves a provider-reconstructed canonical live URL and outputs the received multiplexed stream to a contained FFmpeg pipe. FFmpeg commits local HLS segments atomically. The local viewer reads that playlist; recording copies the very same committed segments into its owned UUID job, never opens another media receiver. Viewer and recorder leases are independent. Four live sessions have a separate admission cap from two VOD workers, avoiding starvation. Each session keeps 12 HLS playlist segments plus six grace segments, at most 32 MiB each (worst-case watch disk budget 2.25 GiB across four sessions), plus one bounded 32 MiB in-progress segment. The chat receiver is session-owned and fans out to a 500-item/1 MiB ring and the current recording archive sink; recording does not create another chat connection. Chat has explicit receipt-time-approximate anchors, missing-anchor fallback, gaps and limits. Watch buffers are disposable after a clean receiver stop; failed archive inputs remain until complete decode/hash verification.
